raw.assessment: The incumbent supplies embedded-caption previews and accessible history on existing infrastructure. It reached the intended preview within 15 minutes in 20/30 sessions. H1-O7 limits a general rendering-failure account: all nine single-correction sessions took five to 11 minutes without reported uncertainty. Multiple saves, out-of-order completion and inconsistent mapping records make version identification a plausible contributor, but do not establish its cause or explain all ten slow sessions. The sampled 49 processing hours do not establish festival capacity. These are stipulated synthetic observations.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: a durable preview identity binding an immutable caption snapshot and video hash, displayed when requesting and downloading, would reduce unintended version selection. Validate the worker inputs against that identity before exposing the artifact.
openings.delta: Replace inference from filenames and completion sequence with one inspectable source pair; retain delivered artifacts and their original caption snapshots.
openings.prediction: With deliberately reversed completion order, editors identify their requested pair correctly; any worker-input mismatch is detected before download. Persistent mistakes despite correct binding would weaken the selection explanation.
openings.probe: In private staging, use demonstration footage and two editors to compare current history with a minimal identity display under reversed completion. Record requested, consumed and downloaded hashes plus identification time. Check that the last delivered wording remains retrievable.
assumptions: Snapshot storage and input verification fit the four engineer-days and existing accounts.
Editors can recognize intended pairs from the displayed identity; installation output stays unchanged.

openings.claim: Do missed deadlines primarily reflect unavailable final-edit artifacts or difficulty identifying and reviewing artifacts already available?
openings.delta: Separate artifact readiness from editor completion before choosing whether to alter render scheduling.
openings.prediction: A scheduling explanation predicts most excess time precedes verified final-pair availability; an identification/review explanation predicts substantial elapsed time afterward.
openings.probe: Align render events with final-edit, verified-pair availability, selection and review timestamps in staged repeated-save and single-correction tasks; record waiting and active work separately within the editor-day.
assumptions: A small staged sample can distinguish large timing differences; it cannot establish the 30-session success target or festival demand.

raw.assessment: Out-of-order completions and unexpected source versions support testing a joint identity-and-scheduling change. They do not establish whether queueing or editor selection accounts for the ten slower sessions. One opening is warranted; meeting the time target remains unproven.

openings.claim: Hypothesis: cross immutable video-caption manifests with generation-aware pending-render coalescing at the save-to-render-queue interface. Each save records both source hashes and a request generation; only the newest pending generation is dispatched. Completion publishes against its captured manifest, while a current-preview pointer advances only to the still-intended generation. Preserve the delivered version and original captions through a separate retained pointer.
openings.delta: Manifest binding alone leaves redundant render demand; coalescing alone cannot establish which video-caption pair a completion contains. Together, the same identity determines both work eligibility and preview eligibility, potentially reducing wasted work without making arrival order stand for editorial intent.
openings.prediction: In multi-save sessions with overlapping jobs, the combination should reduce obsolete renders relative to manifest binding alone and reduce incorrectly identified previews relative to coalescing alone. Jointly correct-and-timely previews should improve most where both overlap and identity confusion occur; little benefit is expected in single-correction sessions. If selection or watching dominates, the time target may remain unmet.
openings.probe: Use fabricated footage and timestamped events in private staging to compare baseline, manifest-only, coalescing-only, and combined behavior under identical rapid-save, reversed-completion, and changed-cut sequences. Measure obsolete dispatches, actual output source hashes, editor identification errors, and waiting versus selection time. Verify retained delivered wording and playable embedded-caption output. Bound implementation to four engineer-days and editor comparison to one editor-day; record processing use. Subsequently evaluate the stated 30-session target: at least 27 correctly identified within 15 minutes and zero unintended combinations.
assumptions: Workers can capture and verify immutable input pairs with a small queue/publication change.
Enough redundant requests remain pending for coalescing to save processing.
Retained manifests and source captions fit existing private storage; staging plus normal work remains within 80 processing hours per week.

openings.claim: Bind immutable caption/video snapshots to a displayed request/download identity; verify worker inputs before publication.
openings.discriminator: Reversed completion still yields correct pair identification; continued mistakes weaken selection causality.
openings.fit: Uncertain implementation cost; retain delivered artifacts and original captions.
openings.probe: Compare current history with identity display; record requested, consumed and downloaded hashes and identification time.
openings.uncertainty: Editors may not recognize intended pairs; snapshot verification must fit budget.

openings.claim: Separate artifact readiness delays from identification and review delays.
openings.discriminator: Excess time before verified final-pair availability supports scheduling; afterward supports selection/review.
openings.probe: Timestamp final edit, verified availability, selection and review; separate waiting/active work across repeated-save and single-correction tasks.
openings.uncertainty: Small staging sample cannot establish session target or festival capacity.

openings.claim: Cross manifests with newest-pending-generation dispatch; publish captured manifests, advance current pointer only for intended generation, and retain delivered pointer separately.
openings.discriminator: Combined behavior reduces obsolete renders versus manifests alone and identification errors versus coalescing alone; little single-correction benefit expected.
openings.fit: Uncertain queue/publication cost and storage/processing headroom.
openings.probe: Compare baseline, manifest-only, coalescing-only and combined under rapid saves, reversed completions and changed cuts; measure obsolete dispatches, output hashes, errors and timing.
openings.uncertainty: Benefit requires redundant pending jobs; selection/watching may still dominate.

post_distill.decision: Probe with demonstration footage and two editors on existing private accounts; cap four engineer-days, one editor-day and 80 processing hours/week. Verify embedded-caption playback and retained delivered wording. Then test 30 sessions: >=27 correctly identified within 15 minutes, zero unintended pairs. Synthetic evidence; observed 49 hours does not establish festival capacity.
